name: Stegomosuchus
isnote: English Wikipedia calls it a protosuchian crocodylomorph (family Stegomosuchidae), but Whetstone and Whybrow (1983) found the only specimen too poorly preserved to classify; kept in Crocodyliformes.
sum: Stegomosuchus is a small crocodylomorph known from one partial skeleton, mostly impressions, from the Early Jurassic Portland Formation of Massachusetts.
wsnote: Skull about 35 mm long; snout-to-pelvis length about 149 mm; Walker regarded the specimen as a juvenile, so no adult range is given.
holotype: AM 900 (Amherst College Museum of Natural History), a partial skeleton preserved mostly as impressions, from the Portland Formation, Hoover Quarry (formerly Hines Quarry), east of East Longmeadow, Massachusetts.
biology: The sources consulted describe the specimen and its classification but give no direct evidence of diet or habits.
author: von Huene 1922

sources.text: von Huene, F. 1922. The Triassic reptilian order Thecodontia. American Journal of Science (5) 4(19): 22–26.
Emerson, B. K. and Loomis, F. B. 1904. On Stegomus longipes, a new reptile from the Triassic sandstones of the Connecticut Valley. American Journal of Science (4) 17(4): 377–380.
Walker, A. D. 1968. Protosuchus, Proterochampsa, and the origin of phytosaurs and crocodiles. Geological Magazine 105(1): 1–14.

Whetstone, K. N. and Whybrow, P. J. 1983. A 'cursorial' crocodilian from the Triassic of Lesotho (Basutoland), southern Africa. Occasional Papers of the Museum of Natural History, University of Kansas 106: 1–37.

dates_note: No PBDB occurrences. English Wikipedia gives the late Hettangian (about 200.5-200 Ma); the whole Hettangian stage of the ICS chart is used here. Originally thought to be Triassic.
